skills_considered.reason: A fingerprinted complete HTML artifact and PDF were supplied; retrieval was limited to figures and supplement status.
The endocrine phenotype opens causal alternatives but does not mature a treatment hypothesis.
No molecule or intervention was proposed.
Canonical promotion and BATCH_COMMIT remain with the operator.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed ESearch on 2026-08-11 returned 137 Aqeilan RI author records and 64 WWOX title/abstract records. The group is primary for WWOX experimental mouse biology and generated the model, but is not a primary disease-clinical or endocrine physiology group. Direct histology, hormone and expression observations are weighted separately from the stronger cell-autonomous interpretation.

queries.query: WWOX AND (mouse OR mice) AND knockout

field_density.note: The steroidogenesis intersection contains only three records, so this paper is unusually load-bearing and sparse rather than broadly replicated.

multihop.note: All 27 references and PMIDs were enumerated. The two assigned foundational mouse papers cited as references 3 and 4 were read in this same batch; no new unresolved load-bearing citation was created.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where does PMID 18974271 occur and how does its endocrine phenotype intersect the systemic-null boundary?
corpus_crossquery.note: Nine disease-model files contain the PMID, including FT-046. The direct endocrine observations add a branch to CLAIM 036, while the pituitary changes and systemic terminal illness prevent a cell-autonomous gonadal interpretation.

retraction_check.result: Repository retraction preflight on 2026-08-11 returned no retraction or expression-of-concern flag for PMID 18974271.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Local PMC HTML identifies PMID 18974271, PMCID PMC2654736 and DOI 10.1210/en.2008-1087 and contains the complete article, Table 1, four captions and 27 references. entries.proposition: Leydig-cell hypoplasia accompanies undetectable serum testosterone in knockout juveniles.
entries.snippet: whereas in WT mice testosterone levels were ranging 50–65 pg/ml (13), in KO mice testosterone levels were undetectable
entries.anchor: Results, Testicular abnormalities and impaired steroidogenesis

entries.proposition: The ovary phenotype is developmentally bounded because death prevents assessment of later follicle maturation.
entries.snippet: Because the KO pups die at juvenile age, we did not study the maturation of the primary follicles toward secondary follicles, graafian follicles, and corpora lutea

entries.proposition: Pituitary Fsh and Lh reduction supplies a non-gonadal causal route for the steroid phenotype.
entries.snippet: Fshb and, to a lesser extent, Lhb expression is down-regulated in pituitary glands of Wwox KO mice
entries.anchor: Results, Reduced expression of Fsh and Lh

entries.proposition: The microarray pooled WT and HET and used a permissive ten-percent FDR ceiling.
entries.snippet: For calculating fold differences, WT and HET mice were grouped together and compared with KO. Data have a 90% level of confidence that the false discovery rate was less than 10%

entries.proposition: The MLTC-1 experiment implicates WW1 but does not reproduce all in-vivo transcript effects.
entries.snippet: No changes were observed in mRNA expression of Hsd17b3, Cyp11a1, and Cyp17a1 after overexpression of Wwox or WwoxY61R
